images.title: 1 km is 1,000 m on a road
images.purpose: Show that a kilometre is 1,000 m on a road strip marked in km, with 7 km written as 7,000 m as in the example.
images.composition: A long road strip with eight km ticks, a bracket on the first km and a bracket on the whole 7 km.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. ROAD: one long flat rectangle, 1050 px wide and 60 px high (x 203 to 1253, y 330 to 390) filled grey #6B7280 with a thin white dashed line through its middle. TICKS: exactly 8 tall tick marks (50 px) under the road at x 203, 353, 503, 653, 803, 953, 1103 and 1253 (y 390 to 440), labelled below in 40 px bold 0 km, 1 km, 2 km, 3 km, 4 km, 5 km, 6 km and 7 km. FIRST KM: one teal #0072B2 bracket above the road from x 203 to x 353 at y 300 with short end strokes (30 px) and the label 1 km = 1,000 m above it in 44 px bold at x 278, y 250. WHOLE ROAD: one amber #E69F00 bracket above, from x 203 to x 1253 at y 200 with short end strokes and the label 7 km = 7 × 1,000 = 7,000 m above it in 48 px bold at x 728, y 150. In all: 1 road, 8 ticks, 2 brackets. All shapes are flat fills with thin dark #2B2B2B outlines (3 px), no shadows and no gradients; all text is dark #1F2937 sans-serif. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
more or fewer than 8 ticks on the road
images.takeaway: 1 km = 1,000 m, so multiply the km by 1,000 to get m.
images.description: A road strip marked 0 km to 7 km with 1 km = 1,000 m on the first km and 7 km = 7,000 m on the whole road.
images.context: Concept image for The Kilometre. It follows the idea of the Let Us Explore text in your maths book (1,000 m = 1 km, kilo stands for thousand) and shows the concept's own example of a path of 7 km (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Count the km ticks with the child. The slip to watch: writing 7 km as 700 m.
